title: getzep/graphiti
summary: A powerful framework for building temporal knowledge graphs that allow AI agents to track evolving facts, relationships, and historical context over time.
risk_notes: Installed via pip. Requires integration with LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) via API keys. As a library, it runs within the user's application process, inheriting its filesystem and network permissions. The project is highly active and well-maintained by the Zep team.

title: katanemo/plano
summary: Plano is an AI-native proxy server and data plane built on Envoy, designed to handle LLM routing, agent orchestration, observability, and guardrails for production agentic applications.
risk_notes: Distributed primarily as a Docker container, which is the recommended and safest deployment method. It acts as a central proxy for LLM traffic, meaning it will handle sensitive API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) and potentially sensitive prompt/response data. It requires careful configuration of network access and environment variables for secrets. The project is actively maintained by core Envoy contributors.

title: superlinked/sie
summary: A comprehensive, self-hosted inference engine that provides an OpenAI-compatible API for a wide range of models, including embedding, reranking, OCR, and LLM generation tasks.
risk_notes: Installs via pip or Docker. Requires significant hardware resources (GPU recommended) and persistent storage for model weights. The server exposes an API that processes data locally, but it will download model weights from Hugging Face, requiring network access. It is designed for production deployment with Kubernetes support.

title: unicodeveloper/consultralph
summary: An AI-powered research agent built with Next.js that automates the creation of consulting-grade deliverables like PDF reports, spreadsheets, and slide decks.
risk_notes: Requires a third-party API key (Valyu) to function. The self-hosted mode is straightforward (Node.js/npm), but it exposes an interface that performs external network requests to the Valyu API. No root access required, but ensure the API key is managed securely in environment variables.

title: booklore-app/booklore
summary: BookLore is a comprehensive, self-hosted digital library management system that supports multi-user access, metadata enrichment, and synchronization with e-readers like Kobo.
risk_notes: Deployed via Docker Compose using official GHCR images. Requires persistent volume access to local storage for book files and a MariaDB database container. It handles sensitive user data and supports OIDC for authentication. The project is actively maintained, though it explicitly warns against using network-attached storage (NAS) for file operations to prevent data corruption.

title: kuberwastaken/claurst
summary: A high-performance, open-source terminal coding agent written in Rust that provides a TUI-based pair programming experience with multi-provider support.
risk_notes: Installs via curl-to-bash or npm/bun global install. As an agentic coding tool, it requires API keys (Anthropic, etc.) and has full read/write access to your local filesystem and shell to execute commands and modify code. It is actively maintained but currently in beta, so caution is advised when granting it execution permissions.

title: adscanpro/adscan
summary: A comprehensive, all-in-one CLI tool for Active Directory penetration testing and security auditing on Linux, consolidating multiple traditional tools into a single workflow.
risk_notes: The tool is installed via pipx and runs entirely within a Docker container, which provides a degree of isolation. However, it requires significant system resources (12GB+ disk) and, by design, performs network-level scanning, credential harvesting, and exploitation of Active Directory environments. It should only be used in authorized, isolated lab or engagement environments as it is an offensive security tool.

title: memvid/claude-brain
summary: A Claude Code plugin that provides persistent, local, long-term memory for AI coding sessions by storing context in a single, portable .mv2 file.
risk_notes: Installs via Claude Code plugin marketplace or npm global install. The tool operates locally on your filesystem and requires read/write access to your project directories to manage the .mv2 memory file. No external API keys are required as it runs locally, and the memory file is portable/git-committable.

title: siderolabs/omni
summary: Omni is a management platform for deploying and operating Kubernetes clusters on bare metal or virtual machines, specifically designed to work with Talos Linux.
risk_notes: Installed via Helm chart on an existing Kubernetes cluster. It requires significant cluster-level permissions to manage nodes and infrastructure. The project uses a Business Source License (BSL-1.1), which restricts production use without a commercial agreement. It is actively maintained by Sidero Labs.

title: rafatosta/zapzap
summary: A feature-rich, open-source desktop client for WhatsApp built with Python and PyQt6, offering native system integration, multi-account support, and cross-platform packaging.
risk_notes: Installs via standard package managers (Flatpak, Snap, DEB) or pip. As a web wrapper, it requires network access to WhatsApp servers and has access to local filesystem for downloads and session storage. It is actively maintained with frequent updates.

title: pguso/rag-from-scratch
summary: An educational, step-by-step guide to building Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines from scratch using Node.js and local LLMs.
risk_notes: The project is a code-based tutorial requiring Node.js and npm. It runs locally and uses node-llama-cpp to execute LLMs on your machine. It requires access to your local filesystem to read documents and write vector stores. No external API keys are required as it emphasizes local-only execution, making it a low-risk, privacy-focused project.

title: alainm23/planify
summary: A modern, feature-rich task manager for GNOME that supports Todoist and self-hosted Nextcloud/CalDAV synchronization.
risk_notes: Distributed primarily via Flathub, which provides a sandboxed environment. Building from source requires standard system dependencies and root access for installation. It handles sensitive credentials for Todoist and CalDAV services, which are managed via libsecret.

title: simoncirstoiu/alice
summary: ALICE is a comprehensive, self-hosted toolkit designed to streamline the YOLO dataset management pipeline, specifically optimized for Frigate NVR users to annotate, train, and export custom object detection models.
risk_notes: The project uses a custom 'builder.py' script to manage virtual environments and dependencies, which is safer than arbitrary shell scripts but still requires execution of local Python code. It requires read/write access to your local filesystem (for dataset storage) and network access to your Frigate NVR instance. The license is 'PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0', which restricts commercial use. It is a very new project (created April 2026), so it should be treated as experimental.

title: toinbox/simplerelay
summary: A self-hosted, multi-tenant SMTP relay service that centralizes outbound email routing, provider management, and access control via a Docker-based stack.
risk_notes: Installed via Docker Compose. Requires exposure of port 2525 (SMTP) and 8080 (Web). The container handles sensitive SMTP credentials for multiple providers and requires a PostgreSQL database. It is a security-sensitive service; misconfiguration could lead to an open relay, though the project explicitly includes IP whitelisting and authentication to mitigate this. Maintenance is active as of June 2026.

title: aeonfun/aeon
summary: An autonomous agent framework designed to run unattended on GitHub Actions, capable of self-improving, scheduling tasks, and executing complex workflows via Markdown-based skill definitions.
risk_notes: Requires GitHub CLI (gh) authentication and extensive permissions to your repositories to perform automated commits, PRs, and deployments. It relies on external LLM API keys (e.g., Anthropic, Grok) and runs unattended in GitHub Actions, which could lead to unexpected costs or repository changes if not properly sandboxed. The installation uses a local script execution pattern after cloning the template.

title: mindmuxai/brain.md
summary: A CLI-based tool that establishes a standardized, persistent Markdown-based memory layer for coding agents to maintain project context, decisions, and constraints across sessions.
risk_notes: The tool is installed via local symlinking of scripts and requires Node.js. It operates directly on your local filesystem within your project directories. It does not inherently require network access or API keys, but it is designed to be invoked by AI coding agents (like Claude Code or Cursor) which may have their own network/API requirements. It is a new, early-stage project (v0.1.0) and should be reviewed for potential side effects on existing project structures.

title: fan-ziqi/robot_viewer
summary: A powerful, browser-based 3D robot visualization and simulation tool supporting URDF, Xacro, and MJCF formats with integrated MuJoCo physics.
risk_notes: Standard Node.js project installation via pnpm/npm. Since it runs entirely in the browser (client-side), it has a very low security footprint; it does not require server-side access to your filesystem or network, and all processing is local to the browser session.

title: sanjay3290/ai-skills
summary: A comprehensive collection of portable 'skills' for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) that enable automation across databases, DevOps tools, and Google Workspace.
risk_notes: Installs via plugin managers (Claude Code marketplace or npx skills). These skills act as bridges to external services (Google Workspace, Atlassian, Azure DevOps, Databases), meaning they require sensitive API keys, OAuth tokens, and database credentials to function. Users must ensure they understand the scope of permissions granted to these agents, as they can perform read/write operations on connected accounts.

title: codingagentsystem/cas
summary: A multi-agent orchestration CLI and MCP server that enables parallelized coding tasks using Claude Code, featuring persistent memory and task management via a local SQLite database.
risk_notes: Installs via shell script (curl | sh) or Homebrew. Requires active Claude Code configuration and API keys. The tool performs filesystem operations by creating git worktrees and modifying codebases, and it requires network access to communicate with Anthropic's API. It is actively maintained with recent commits.

title: owloops/updo
summary: A versatile Go-based CLI tool for website uptime monitoring that supports local TUI-based checks, multi-region AWS Lambda deployment, and Prometheus/Grafana integration.
risk_notes: Offers multiple installation methods including Homebrew, package managers, and a curl-to-bash script (use with caution). Requires network access to target URLs and potentially AWS credentials if using the multi-region Lambda feature. The project is actively maintained and written in Go, which is generally memory-safe.

title: aaronjmars/aeon
summary: An autonomous agent framework designed to run unattended on GitHub Actions, capable of scheduling tasks, self-improving its own skills, and performing complex workflows like code deployment and vulnerability research.
risk_notes: Requires GitHub CLI (gh) for setup and relies on GitHub Actions for execution. It necessitates providing various LLM API keys and potentially sensitive credentials for integrations (Telegram, Discord, etc.). Because it is designed for 'no approval' autonomous operation, it has the potential to modify repositories and execute code unattended; users should carefully audit the 'skills' (Markdown files) before deployment to ensure they do not perform unintended actions.

title: lackeyjb/playwright-skill
summary: A Claude Code plugin that enables the AI to autonomously write and execute Playwright browser automation scripts for testing and web interaction tasks.
risk_notes: Requires installation via Claude Code's plugin system or manual file placement. It executes arbitrary Node.js code generated by the LLM, which has access to your local filesystem and network. Users should be aware that granting an LLM control over a browser and local execution environment carries inherent security risks; ensure you review the generated scripts before execution if performing sensitive tasks.

title: sysadminsmedia/homebox
summary: A lightweight, high-performance inventory management system written in Go, designed for home users to track assets, warranties, and maintenance.
risk_notes: Distributed as a Docker container via GHCR. Supports rootless and hardened images, which is a strong security practice. Requires persistent volume mapping for SQLite data. No external API keys required for core functionality; runs entirely locally.

title: kittendevv/invio
summary: A minimalist, self-hosted invoicing application designed for simplicity and privacy, allowing users to generate and share invoices without account requirements for clients.
risk_notes: Typically deployed via Docker/Containerization which is standard for self-hosting. Requires database connectivity and persistent storage for invoice data. As a web-facing application, it requires proper reverse proxy configuration and security hardening to prevent unauthorized access to financial records.

title: roboparty/roboto_origin
summary: A comprehensive, fully open-source project providing hardware designs, firmware, and ROS2-based software for building a DIY humanoid robot.
risk_notes: Requires physical hardware assembly and custom firmware flashing to embedded controllers (OrangePi/RDK). Software stack relies on ROS2 Humble and NVIDIA Isaac Sim, which are complex environments. No automated 'curl | sudo' install scripts are apparent, but it requires deep system-level access to hardware interfaces and motor controllers.

title: mightymoud/sidekick
summary: A CLI tool that simplifies VPS management by automating Docker, Traefik, and SOPS configuration to provide a Heroku-like deployment experience on bare metal.
risk_notes: The tool requires SSH access to your VPS and performs administrative tasks including creating a new sudo user, disabling root login, and installing system-wide packages like Docker and Traefik. It is installed via Homebrew. It handles sensitive environment variables using SOPS/age encryption, which is a strong security practice, but it requires full control over your server's configuration.

title: x011/smtp-tunnel-proxy
summary: A covert tunnel proxy that encapsulates TCP traffic within SMTP-like sessions to bypass restrictive DPI firewalls.
risk_notes: The installation uses a 'curl | sudo bash' script, which grants the installer full root privileges on the host machine. The tool requires opening port 587 and managing TLS certificates, which involves modifying system-level network configurations. It acts as a SOCKS5 proxy, meaning it has the potential to intercept or redirect all traffic routed through it if misconfigured.

title: amaancoderx/npxskillui
summary: A powerful CLI tool that reverse-engineers design systems from websites or codebases into structured documentation and assets optimized for Claude Code to generate UI components.
risk_notes: Installed via npm (npm install -g skillui). Requires Node.js 18+. The 'ultra' mode uses Playwright, which executes browser automation. It performs network requests to target URLs and reads/writes to the local filesystem. It does not require API keys, as it performs static analysis and local scraping.

title: jasonxtn/argus
summary: Argus is a comprehensive, modular Python-based reconnaissance and information-gathering toolkit designed for security analysts to perform network, web, and threat intelligence assessments.
risk_notes: The tool requires network access to perform scans and lookups. It can be installed via pip or run via Docker, which is the recommended approach for isolation. It relies on various external APIs (e.g., Shodan, Censys) which may require user-provided API keys. The 'full installation' script (install.sh) should be audited before execution as it may modify system-level dependencies.

title: krishmunot/awesome-startup
summary: A static list of books, courses, and resources for startup founders.
risk_notes: This is a documentation-only repository containing markdown links. There is no code to execute, so there are no security risks related to installation or system access.

title: adrianhajdin/ghost-ai
summary: An educational project repository designed to accompany a YouTube tutorial on building an AI-powered collaborative system architecture tool.
risk_notes: This is a tutorial codebase, not a production-ready tool. It requires multiple third-party SaaS integrations (Clerk, Liveblocks, Trigger.dev, Google Gemini) and a PostgreSQL database. It is intended for learning purposes rather than deployment in a secure home-lab environment.

title: jxlarrea/voice-satellite-card-integration
summary: A powerful Home Assistant integration that transforms any browser or Android tablet into a fully functional, private voice assistant satellite with local wake-word detection.
risk_notes: Installed via HACS (Home Assistant Community Store), which is the standard, safe method for HA integrations. It requires browser microphone permissions and access to your Home Assistant instance's API. It is actively maintained and aligns with local-first privacy goals.

title: rsmdt/the-startup
summary: A framework for Claude Code that introduces spec-driven development and multi-agent workflows to automate software engineering tasks.
risk_notes: Uses a curl-to-shell installation script which is a security risk; manual installation via Claude Code plugin commands is safer. As an AI agent framework, it requires full read/write access to your local filesystem and your Claude API credentials to function.

title: prod-forge/backend
summary: Prod Forge is a comprehensive, production-grade reference architecture for NestJS backends, focusing on CI/CD, observability, and AI-assisted development workflows.
risk_notes: This is a reference architecture/template, not a standalone tool. It requires significant AWS infrastructure (RDS, ECS, ElastiCache) and configuration. It is intended for developers to study or adapt, so it does not have a simple install script, but it does require managing cloud credentials and environment variables for deployment.

title: wh-2099/mermaid-skill
summary: A specialized skill for Claude Code that enables the generation of 23 different types of Mermaid diagrams directly within the AI agent's workflow.
risk_notes: Installation involves manual file copying or git submodules into a local .claude/skills directory. It runs within the Claude Code environment, meaning it inherits the permissions granted to the Claude agent, including filesystem access. No external network calls are made by the skill itself, as it relies on the LLM's internal knowledge and the provided reference documentation.

title: adithya-s-k/omniparse
summary: OmniParse is a powerful, local-first ingestion and parsing platform designed to convert unstructured data (documents, media, web) into structured formats optimized for GenAI and RAG pipelines.
risk_notes: Requires Linux-based environment. Installation via Docker or pip/poetry. Runs as a local server; requires significant system resources (GPU recommended for performance). As it processes arbitrary files and web content, it should be run in an isolated container or environment to mitigate risks from malicious file inputs or web crawling.

title: tetheria/aero-hand-open
summary: An open-source, tendon-driven robotic hand platform designed for research and hobbyist robotics, featuring 3D-printable parts and a Python SDK.
risk_notes: Requires physical assembly and custom electronics (ESP32). Software is installed via standard Python package management (pip). No inherent network risks beyond standard serial/USB communication with the hardware controller. Maintenance is active.

title: cerno-ai/cerno-agentic-local-deep-research
summary: Cerno is a local-first, agentic research platform that orchestrates multi-step workflows using both cloud-based and local LLMs, providing transparency into reasoning steps and data sovereignty.
risk_notes: Installation via Docker Compose is standard and isolated. The application requires API keys for cloud LLMs (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) and has read/write access to the local filesystem for research artifacts and knowledge sources. It runs a Django backend and React frontend, which should be secured if exposed to a network.

title: neo4j-labs/llm-graph-builder
summary: A powerful tool for building Knowledge Graphs from unstructured data sources like PDFs and web pages using LLMs and Neo4j.
risk_notes: Requires a Neo4j database instance and various third-party LLM API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.). Installation is via standard Python pip requirements or Docker Compose. It handles sensitive data ingestion from local files, S3, and GCS, so it requires careful management of environment variables and access credentials.

title: inlitx/obsidian-dashboard-gallery
summary: A collection of aesthetic and functional dashboard templates for Obsidian, utilizing the Dataview plugin for dynamic content.
risk_notes: Installation involves manually copying .md and .css files into your local Obsidian vault. Some templates require enabling JavaScript in the Dataview plugin, which allows arbitrary code execution within your vault. Some dashboards require external API keys (e.g., OpenWeatherMap) to function.

title: thecmdguy/ducky
summary: Ducky is a comprehensive, all-in-one desktop GUI application built with Python and PySide6 that aggregates various network diagnostic, security, and utility tools into a single interface.
risk_notes: Installed via standard pip/venv workflow. The application requires network access for its diagnostic features (ping, port scanning, DNS lookups) and may require elevated privileges on some operating systems to perform specific network operations like raw packet sniffing or ARP table access. The codebase is Python-based and open-source, allowing for local audit.

title: agentic-box/memora
summary: Memora is an MCP-compliant memory layer for AI agents that provides persistent, structured storage using SQLite, semantic search, and knowledge graph visualization.
risk_notes: Installed via pip. Requires API keys for LLM/embedding providers (OpenAI) and potentially Cloudflare/AWS credentials if using cloud sync. It accesses local filesystems for SQLite storage and runs as an MCP server, which grants the connected AI agent read/write access to the memory database.

title: davunt/app-eraser
summary: An open-source Electron-based macOS utility designed to perform clean uninstalls by identifying and removing leftover application support files and caches.
risk_notes: Distributed as a pre-built DMG; requires elevated macOS permissions including 'Automation' (Finder access) and 'Files and Folders' access to scan and delete files across the system. Maintenance has been slow since late 2023.

title: ahmedbafkir/dlipa
summary: An iOS application that allows users to download and sideload IPA files from the App Store using their Apple ID credentials.
risk_notes: Requires providing Apple ID credentials directly to the app, which poses a significant security risk. Installation requires sideloading via AltStore or similar tools, bypassing standard App Store security checks. The project is not open source (no license, no source code provided in the repo), which prevents auditing of how credentials are handled.

title: bluewave-labs/checkmate
summary: Checkmate is a robust, self-hosted infrastructure and uptime monitoring platform that provides real-time visualizations and supports remote server metrics via an optional Go-based agent.
risk_notes: Installation is performed via Docker Compose, which is standard and secure. The application requires a MongoDB instance and environment variables for authentication (JWT_SECRET). It is designed to monitor external services and remote servers (via the 'Capture' agent), meaning it will have network access to your infrastructure and potentially sensitive system metrics if the agent is deployed on your hosts.

title: boltzmannentropy/mimikastudio
summary: A local-first macOS application leveraging Apple Silicon's MLX for high-performance voice cloning, TTS, and audiobook generation with MCP support for automation.
risk_notes: Distributed as a macOS binary; requires local filesystem access for document processing and audio output. Uses local-first MLX models, minimizing network exposure, but requires downloading large model weights. License is BSL-1.1, which is more restrictive than standard open-source licenses.

title: nhas/reverse_ssh
summary: A powerful SSH-based reverse shell and remote management tool that allows managing multiple remote targets using standard SSH syntax, SCP, and SFTP.
risk_notes: This is a high-risk security tool designed for remote command execution. It requires running a server component (typically via Docker) and deploying client binaries to target machines. It supports fileless execution and provides full shell access, making it a powerful tool for authorized penetration testing but a significant security risk if misconfigured or used maliciously. It is actively maintained.

title: lraton/flopperziro
summary: A DIY, open-source hardware multi-tool project based on the STM32 microcontroller, designed to replicate Flipper Zero functionality for hobbyists.
risk_notes: Requires custom PCB assembly and soldering. Software is flashed via Arduino IDE, which involves compiling and uploading C++ code to the microcontroller. As a hardware tool capable of RF/NFC/IR signal manipulation, it requires physical access to target devices and carries inherent risks associated with radio frequency transmission and hardware-level security testing.

title: ni5arga/sightline
summary: Sightline is a specialized OSINT search engine that leverages OpenStreetMap and the Overpass API to map and analyze critical infrastructure like power plants, telecom towers, and industrial facilities.
risk_notes: The project is a TypeScript web application. It relies on public APIs (Nominatim, Overpass) and does not require local root access. It is designed to be self-hosted or deployed via Vercel; users should be aware of potential rate limits imposed by the public OSM APIs if running high-volume queries.

title: ix-infrastructure/ix
summary: Ix is a developer tool that creates a persistent, structured map of your codebase to improve LLM reasoning and developer navigation, significantly reducing token usage.
risk_notes: Installation uses curl-to-shell scripts, which is a common but high-trust pattern requiring execution of remote code. The tool requires Docker/Docker Compose for its local backend and will have read access to your entire codebase to build its index. It is currently in alpha status, suggesting potential stability issues.

title: spesrobotics/teleop
summary: A Python-based teleoperation framework that uses WebXR to turn mobile devices or VR headsets into controllers for robotic arms, with native support for ROS 2.
risk_notes: Installed via pip. Runs a local server on port 5000 to receive sensor data from mobile devices over the network. Requires careful network configuration if exposed. Relies on external dependencies like Pinocchio for kinematics. Active maintenance status is good.

title: kamranahmedse/slim
summary: A developer-focused CLI tool for managing local HTTPS domains and exposing local services to the internet via secure tunnels.
risk_notes: Installs via curl-to-sh script, which is a common but risky pattern. Requires root/sudo privileges to modify /etc/hosts and manage system-level CA certificates for HTTPS. The 'share' feature requires authentication and creates a public tunnel, which exposes local services to the internet.

title: alexanderwanyoike/the0
summary: An open-source, self-hosted algorithmic trading execution engine that supports multiple programming languages and includes an MCP server for AI-assisted management.
risk_notes: Installation uses a curl-to-shell script, which requires caution. The platform is designed to manage financial assets, requiring sensitive API keys for exchanges and database credentials. It runs via Docker Compose or Kubernetes, necessitating careful management of secrets and network exposure for the dashboard and API.

title: karanb192/awesome-claude-skills
summary: A curated, community-driven collection of modular 'skills' for Claude Code and the Claude ecosystem, designed to extend agent capabilities for development, debugging, and automation tasks.
risk_notes: Installation involves cloning git repositories into a local ~/.claude/skills directory. Since these skills are essentially instructions and scripts that Claude executes, they have the potential to interact with your local filesystem and execute code on your machine if you grant Claude Code those permissions. Review the contents of any cloned skill before usage, as they can execute arbitrary commands within the context of your development environment.

title: qosf/awesome-quantum-software
summary: A comprehensive curated list of open-source quantum computing software, libraries, and frameworks.
risk_notes: This is a documentation-only repository (a list of links). It does not contain executable code, so there are no installation risks or system access requirements. It is well-maintained and serves as a reference index.

title: reconmap/reconmap
summary: Reconmap is a comprehensive, self-hosted security operations platform that streamlines penetration testing workflows, command automation, and vulnerability reporting.
risk_notes: Installs via Docker Compose, which is a standard and safe deployment method. As a security platform, it requires network access to target systems and will store sensitive vulnerability data, so it should be deployed in a secure, isolated environment. The project is actively maintained.

title: postgres-ai/database-lab-engine
summary: DBLab Engine provides high-performance thin cloning and branching for PostgreSQL, enabling developers to create full-scale database environments for testing, CI/CD, and query optimization.
risk_notes: Requires significant system resources and filesystem access to manage ZFS/LVM snapshots for cloning. It typically runs as a service (often via Docker/Kubernetes) and requires administrative access to the database instance or a dedicated VM with network connectivity to the source database. Maintenance is active and professional.

title: magnum6actual/flipoff
summary: A lightweight, dependency-free web application that emulates a mechanical split-flap display for use on TVs or monitors.
risk_notes: Extremely low risk. It is a static HTML/JS project with no external dependencies, build tools, or server-side requirements. It runs entirely in the browser and requires no special permissions or network access.

title: vercel-labs/knowledge-agent-template
summary: A powerful, deterministic AI agent template that uses file-system tools (grep, find, cat) instead of vector databases, allowing for transparent and accurate knowledge retrieval.
risk_notes: Designed for deployment on Vercel; requires GitHub OAuth credentials and various API keys (LLM providers). It utilizes isolated sandboxes for command execution, which mitigates some risks, but the agent has access to the provided data sources and potentially sensitive environment variables. Maintenance is active as it is a Vercel Labs project.

title: trevtron/rtl-ml
summary: An AI-powered radio signal classification pipeline designed for ARM SBCs like the Raspberry Pi, using RTL-SDR hardware to identify various radio signals locally.
risk_notes: Requires building custom drivers from source (cmake/make/sudo make install) which modifies system-level udev rules and kernel module blacklists. Runs as a standard Python application in a virtual environment. Accesses USB hardware directly via librtlsdr. No sensitive credentials or network exposure required by default.

title: pikpikcu/airecon
summary: AIRecon is an autonomous, privacy-focused penetration testing agent that runs locally using Ollama and Docker, providing a full recon-to-report pipeline without cloud dependencies.
risk_notes: Requires Docker for the Kali sandbox and Ollama for local LLM execution. It performs active network reconnaissance and exploitation, meaning it has full access to the host's network and the filesystem where it stores session data. It is designed for security professionals and should be run in an isolated environment (e.g., a dedicated VM or container) to prevent accidental damage to local systems or unauthorized network activity.

title: fsoft-ai4code/codewiki
summary: CodeWiki is an AI-powered CLI tool that generates structured, architecture-aware documentation for large-scale codebases, supporting multiple LLM providers and subscription-based CLI integrations.
risk_notes: Installed via pip. Requires API keys for various LLM providers or integration with local CLI tools (Claude/Codex). It performs deep analysis of local codebases, meaning it requires read access to your project files and sends code context to external LLM APIs. Users should be mindful of sensitive data in their repositories before running.

title: serengil/deepface
summary: A comprehensive, lightweight Python framework for face recognition and facial attribute analysis that wraps multiple state-of-the-art deep learning models.
risk_notes: Installed via pip or source. Requires access to local filesystem for image processing and model weights. Downloads pre-trained model weights from the internet upon first use. As a library, it runs with the permissions of the user executing the script; no special root privileges are required.

title: tbxark/mail2telegram
summary: A serverless Cloudflare Worker that integrates with Cloudflare Email Routing to forward incoming emails to a Telegram bot, supporting temporary mailboxes and email backups.
risk_notes: Requires deployment to Cloudflare Workers and providing a Telegram Bot API token. The worker handles incoming email traffic and interacts with the Telegram API. It uses Cloudflare KV for storage. No local root access required, but it acts as a bridge for your email traffic.

title: adrianhajdin/roomify
summary: An educational project repository designed to accompany a YouTube tutorial on building an AI-powered architectural visualization app using the Puter cloud platform.
risk_notes: This is a tutorial-based codebase rather than a production-ready tool. It relies on the Puter cloud platform and requires external API keys for AI services (Claude/Gemini). It is not intended for self-hosting in a home-lab environment and lacks a clear security audit or maintenance lifecycle.

title: agricidaniel/skill-forge
summary: A CLI-based framework for designing, scaffolding, and benchmarking AI agent skills specifically for the Claude Code ecosystem.
risk_notes: Installation uses a bash script which clones the repo and likely sets up local paths; requires manual review of the install.sh script. The tool interacts with local filesystems to scaffold and manage AI skills, and it is designed to interface with Claude Code, which may have broad access to your local environment and API keys.

title: lissy93/web-check
summary: A comprehensive, self-hostable OSINT dashboard that aggregates various network and security diagnostics for any given website.
risk_notes: Can be deployed via Docker, which is the recommended secure path. It performs external network requests to analyze target sites, so it should be run in an isolated container. It does not require root access, but be mindful of the data it exposes if you host it publicly.

title: btseytlin/hr-breaker
summary: An AI-powered resume optimization tool that uses LLMs and multi-stage validation filters to tailor resumes for specific job descriptions, offering both a CLI and a FastAPI-based web interface.
