title: happycerberus/book-cpp-algorithms
summary: A comprehensive, high-quality open-source book covering Standard C++ algorithms, including C++20 ranges and views, with verifiable code examples.
risk_notes: The repository is a documentation project. It provides a Docker-based devcontainer for building the LaTeX source, which is a safe, isolated way to handle dependencies. No sensitive permissions or network access are required for the code samples themselves, which are designed for local compilation and verification.

title: nicolargo/glances
summary: A comprehensive, cross-platform system monitoring tool that provides a TUI, web dashboard, and REST/MCP API for real-time performance tracking.
risk_notes: Installable via pip or Docker. Requires read access to system metrics (CPU, memory, disk, processes), which may require elevated privileges depending on the OS and specific metrics requested. The web server mode exposes an API; ensure it is secured behind a reverse proxy or firewall if exposed to a network.

title: oven-sh/awesome-bun
summary: A comprehensive, community-maintained collection of resources, frameworks, and tools for the Bun JavaScript runtime.
risk_notes: This is a documentation/curation repository and contains no executable code itself. It links to external third-party projects; users should exercise standard caution when installing dependencies or running code from linked repositories, as those may require network access, filesystem permissions, or API keys.

title: gautamkrishnar/nothing-private
summary: A proof-of-concept project demonstrating how browser fingerprinting can track users across incognito sessions using Client.js, PHP, and MySQL.
risk_notes: This is a web application requiring a LAMP stack (PHP/MySQL). It is intended for educational/demonstration purposes. Running this on a public server requires standard web security practices; it is not a tool to be installed on a local machine as a utility, but rather a reference implementation for understanding tracking vectors.

title: conduitplatform/conduit
summary: Conduit is a self-hosted, modular backend-as-a-service platform that provides pre-built modules for authentication, database management, and API generation to accelerate development.
risk_notes: Installation involves a curl-to-shell script which poses security risks; it requires Docker and Docker Compose to run. As a backend platform, it handles sensitive user data, authentication, and database connections, requiring careful configuration of secrets and network access.

title: shannhk/llm-wikid
summary: An AI-driven knowledge management system for Obsidian that uses LLM agents to ingest, classify, and cross-link raw data sources into a structured wiki.
risk_notes: Requires granting an LLM agent (like Claude Code) full read/write access to your local filesystem and potentially network access for web scraping/API calls. The project relies on external agent tools (Claude Code, yt-dlp, etc.) which must be installed separately. Security depends entirely on the permissions granted to the agent; the README explicitly suggests running with elevated permissions, which should be handled with caution.

title: hughkli/lookin
summary: Lookin is a powerful, free macOS application for inspecting and modifying iOS UI components in real-time, serving as an open-source alternative to tools like Reveal.
risk_notes: Requires integrating the LookinServer framework into your iOS project via CocoaPods or Swift Package Manager. It is critical to restrict this to Debug builds only to prevent security vulnerabilities in production apps. The macOS app is a standard GUI application; no root access or unusual permissions are required beyond standard developer tool access.

title: 0xmr007/lab4purplesec
summary: A comprehensive, modular Purple Team homelab environment that automates the deployment of vulnerable Active Directory, DMZ, firewall, and SIEM components for security training.
risk_notes: The project uses Vagrant and Ansible to automate the deployment of multiple virtual machines. It requires significant system resources (RAM/Disk) and hypervisor access (VirtualBox/VMware). Because it builds a vulnerable environment, it should be run in an isolated network segment to prevent accidental exposure of the vulnerable services to the host or local network.

title: ominousindustries/phonedriver
summary: An automation agent that leverages Qwen3-VL vision models to control Android devices via ADB, allowing for natural language task execution.
risk_notes: Requires ADB access to an Android device, which grants the script full control over the device's UI and input. Installation involves standard pip dependencies and cloning from GitHub. The tool runs locally, but requires significant GPU VRAM to host the Qwen3-VL model. Users should be aware that granting ADB access to a script allows it to perform any action a user can, including interacting with sensitive apps.

title: pranavp10/video-compress
summary: A Next.js-based web application that leverages FFmpeg to provide a local, browser-based video compression tool.
risk_notes: Requires Bun runtime for local development. As a web-based tool, it processes files locally in the browser via FFmpeg (WASM), which is generally secure as it avoids server-side uploads. The license explicitly requests not to copy the code directly, which is a non-standard restriction for an MIT-licensed repo.

title: eldavoo/wa-crypt-tools
summary: A Python-based CLI suite for decrypting and encrypting WhatsApp backup files (.crypt12, .crypt14, .crypt15), useful for data recovery and local backup management.
risk_notes: Installed via pip. Requires access to sensitive local files (WhatsApp backup databases and encryption keys). The encryption functionality is marked as beta and requires careful handling of keys. The tool is intended for local use and does not inherently require network access, but users should be cautious when handling private keys.

title: awesome-scripts/awesome-userscripts
summary: A comprehensive, curated list of high-quality userscripts for enhancing browser functionality, privacy, and automation across various popular web platforms.
risk_notes: Userscripts are installed via browser extensions like Tampermonkey or Violentmonkey. They run within the browser's context and can access page content, cookies, and perform network requests on your behalf. Users should review the source code of any individual script before installation, as they can potentially exfiltrate data or perform unauthorized actions on the sites they are scoped to.

title: minthcm/minthcm
summary: An open-source, AI-native Human Capital Management (HCM) platform built on top of the SuiteCRM framework, designed for self-hosting and agentic workflows.
risk_notes: Distributed via Docker, which is a standard and secure deployment method. As an HR system, it requires access to sensitive employee data and PII, necessitating strict network isolation and database security. It is actively maintained, but relies on a legacy PHP/CRM codebase, which may have a larger attack surface than modern microservices.

title: jingsongliujing/onnxocr
summary: A high-performance, framework-agnostic OCR and document analysis toolkit that uses ONNXRuntime for inference, supporting tasks like text recognition, table extraction, and structured data parsing via local LLMs.
risk_notes: Installation is via standard pip requirements.txt. The project requires downloading large model files from external sources (HuggingFace/ModelScope), which involves network access. It runs locally on the filesystem and does not require root privileges, but it executes arbitrary model weights which should be handled with standard caution.

title: ogkalu2/comic-translate
summary: An AI-powered application and browser extension that automates the translation of comics and manga using SOTA LLMs for text translation and computer vision for detection and inpainting.
risk_notes: Requires API keys for LLM services (e.g., OpenAI/GPT) to function. The desktop application requires running unsigned binaries (bypassing OS security warnings), which is a standard but non-ideal security practice. Running from source via 'uv' is safer but requires installing multiple dependencies and potentially GPU drivers. The app has access to local files for processing and requires network access to communicate with translation APIs.

title: ivanceras/svgbob
summary: A high-quality Rust-based CLI tool that converts ASCII art diagrams into clean, professional SVG files.
risk_notes: Installed via cargo (cargo install svgbob) or system package managers. It is a local CLI tool that processes text files and outputs SVGs, requiring no network access or special permissions. It is actively maintained and widely used in documentation pipelines.

title: yefga/switzy
summary: A macOS menu bar utility for managing Git identities and SSH configurations, designed to simplify switching between personal and work profiles.
risk_notes: Installed via Homebrew cask or manual DMG download. As a macOS app, it requires filesystem access to modify ~/.gitconfig and ~/.ssh/config files. It is actively maintained and uses standard macOS notarization, but users should review the configuration files it manages to ensure no unintended credential exposure.

title: kostard/esp32s3-usb-keyboard-to-ble
summary: A firmware project for ESP32-S3 boards that acts as a hardware bridge to convert any wired USB keyboard into a multi-device Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) wireless keyboard.
risk_notes: Requires flashing firmware via PlatformIO to an ESP32-S3 microcontroller. The code runs at the firmware level, meaning it has full control over HID input signals. It does not require network access, but it handles Bluetooth pairing data. Hardware setup requires careful attention to power delivery (VBUS) to avoid damaging the ESP32 or the keyboard.

title: opnform/opnform
summary: A robust, open-source form builder built with Laravel and Nuxt, offering a self-hostable alternative to services like Typeform or Google Forms.
risk_notes: Self-hosted via Docker, which is the standard and secure deployment method. Requires a database (PostgreSQL) and environment configuration. As a form builder, it handles user-submitted data, so it requires careful exposure to the internet and proper security headers/firewalling. The project uses a dual-license model (AGPLv3 for core, proprietary for enterprise features).

title: samwillis/solidtype
summary: A modern, collaborative parametric CAD platform built with OpenCascade.js, ElectricSQL, and TanStack, demonstrating advanced real-time sync and AI-assisted modeling.
risk_notes: Requires Docker/Docker Compose for local infrastructure (PostgreSQL, ElectricSQL, Durable Streams). Installation involves standard pnpm workflows. The application handles local database credentials via environment variables and requires network access for sync services. No dangerous install scripts, but it is a complex stack with multiple moving parts.

title: renatoworks/3dsvg
summary: A React-based library and web editor for converting SVGs into interactive 3D components using Three.js and React Three Fiber.
risk_notes: Installed via npm/yarn. Runs entirely in the browser (client-side) or as a React component dependency. Uses FFmpeg WASM for local video processing, which is sandboxed. No sensitive system permissions or backend secrets required.

title: minsang-alt/pasteclip
summary: A lightweight, open-source clipboard manager for macOS built with Swift 6 and SwiftData that prioritizes local-only privacy.
risk_notes: Installed via Homebrew cask or DMG. As a clipboard manager, it requires Accessibility permissions to monitor system-wide copy events and paste content. It is not notarized, requiring manual security overrides on macOS. It is local-only with no network dependencies, which is a positive privacy signal.

title: skavngr/rapidscan
summary: A wrapper script that orchestrates various security scanning tools like nmap and nikto to automate web vulnerability reconnaissance.
risk_notes: Requires installation via pip or cloning into /opt/. It acts as a wrapper for numerous external security tools, meaning it requires those tools to be pre-installed on the host system (typically Kali Linux). It performs active network scanning and requires execution permissions to run network-intensive tasks. Maintenance appears to have slowed significantly since 2023.

title: bee-san/pywhat
summary: A powerful CLI tool for identifying and extracting structured data (like API keys, crypto addresses, and emails) from text, files, and PCAP captures.
risk_notes: Installed via pip or brew. It requires read access to any files or directories you point it at. It is a local tool, but when used to scan network traffic or external files, it processes potentially sensitive data. It is a mature project but has not seen significant updates since late 2023.

title: textualize/frogmouth
summary: A terminal-based Markdown browser built with the Textual framework, offering a GUI-like experience for reading documentation directly in the CLI.
risk_notes: Installs via pipx, pip, or Homebrew, which is standard and safe. It requires read access to local files and network access to fetch remote Markdown files (e.g., from GitHub). Maintained by the active Textualize team.

title: ashish0kumar/windots
summary: A comprehensive collection of configuration files and dotfiles for customizing the Windows 11 environment to feel like a Unix-like tiling window manager setup.
risk_notes: This is a configuration repository, not an executable installer. Users must manually copy files to their local Windows configuration directories (e.g., AppData). It relies on third-party tools like GlazeWM and YASB, which require administrative privileges to modify system UI elements. No automated scripts are provided, reducing the risk of malicious execution, but users should review the config files for hardcoded paths or sensitive environment variables before applying them.

title: openvglab/omnilottie
summary: OmniLottie is a multi-modal generative AI model capable of creating complex Lottie vector animations from text, image, or video instructions.
risk_notes: Requires a dedicated Conda environment and significant GPU resources (15.2GB+ VRAM). Installation involves standard pip packages and downloading large model weights (8.46GB) from HuggingFace. As with any local LLM/VLM, it requires access to your local filesystem to save generated outputs and model weights.

title: bernaferrari/figmatocode
summary: A privacy-focused Figma plugin that converts design elements into clean, framework-specific code (React, Tailwind, Flutter, SwiftUI) without external API calls or AI inference.
risk_notes: Installed via the Figma Community platform. The plugin is highly secure by design; it explicitly requests zero network permissions and runs entirely within the Figma sandbox, meaning it cannot exfiltrate design data or access local files outside of the Figma environment.

title: moktavizen/material-darker-jdownloader
summary: A manual theme customization package for JDownloader 2 that replaces UI assets and configuration files to provide a Material Darker aesthetic.
risk_notes: Installation requires manual file replacement within the JDownloader application directory and importing a configuration backup file. This involves modifying core application files and potentially overwriting existing settings, which carries a risk of breaking the application or losing configurations if not backed up properly.

title: sudhakar3697/awesome-electron-alternatives
summary: A comprehensive, well-maintained curated list of frameworks and tools that serve as alternatives to Electron for cross-platform desktop application development.
risk_notes: This is a documentation-only repository (a markdown list). There is no code to execute, install, or provide permissions to, making it inherently safe to browse. It is actively maintained.

title: tracefinity/tracefinity
summary: A self-hostable tool that uses AI to trace tool outlines from photos and generate custom Gridfinity 3D-printable storage bins.
risk_notes: Distributed as a Docker container, which is a secure and isolated installation method. Requires access to a local data volume for storage. Optional integration with third-party AI APIs (Gemini, Replicate, fal.ai) requires providing API keys, which introduces external data dependency. Local tracing models are available for privacy-conscious users. Actively maintained with clear documentation.

title: xororz/local-dream
summary: An Android application that enables local Stable Diffusion inference by leveraging Snapdragon NPU acceleration, as well as CPU/GPU fallback.
risk_notes: Installed via Google Play Store or APK sideloading. Requires standard Android permissions for storage access to save generated images. Uses native C++ libraries (QNN SDK, MNN) for hardware acceleration, which is typical for high-performance mobile AI apps. Actively maintained with a clear open-source codebase.

title: mendrik-private/sqv
summary: A keyboard-first, TUI-based SQLite database viewer written in Rust, featuring fast virtual scrolling, in-place editing, and foreign-key navigation.
risk_notes: The project provides pre-built Debian packages and binaries. Installation requires sudo privileges to place the binary in system directories. As a local database viewer, it requires read/write access to the SQLite files you point it to. The code is written in Rust, which is generally memory-safe, and the repository shows active maintenance and clear CI/CD practices.

title: unchihugo/fluentflyout
summary: A modern, open-source replacement for Windows 11 system flyouts (media, lock keys, volume) that utilizes Fluent 2 design principles for a native look and feel.
risk_notes: Distributed via Microsoft Store or manual .msixbundle installation. As a system-level utility, it requires permissions to monitor media playback and system input (lock keys). It is actively maintained, but users should be aware that it hooks into system UI processes, which carries inherent stability risks for Windows shell components.

title: remnawave/panel
summary: Remnawave is a proxy management panel built on Xray-core designed to simplify the deployment and administration of censorship-resistant network protocols.
risk_notes: Requires running as a service, likely with elevated privileges to manage network interfaces and Xray-core binaries. Installation typically involves Docker or direct binary execution; requires careful configuration of network ports and potentially sensitive credentials for proxy authentication. Active maintenance is observed.

title: samyak2403/repostore
summary: An Android application that acts as a curated app store for GitHub-hosted projects, allowing users to discover, install, and update APKs directly from release assets.
risk_notes: Distributed via F-Droid and GitHub releases. Requires standard Android permissions for package installation and network access. Optional GitHub OAuth login increases API rate limits but grants the app access to your GitHub profile data. As it installs APKs from third-party GitHub repositories, users should exercise caution regarding the security of the individual apps being installed.

title: aetherinox/ntfy-desktop
summary: A cross-platform Electron-based desktop client for the ntfy.sh push notification service, allowing users to receive alerts from self-hosted or public instances without keeping a browser tab open.
risk_notes: Distributed as pre-built binaries (EXE, DEB, AppImage, DMG) or via source build. Requires network access to connect to ntfy instances. Electron apps have access to the local filesystem and system notification APIs. The project provides signed releases and checksums, which is a good security practice.

title: nab138/iloader
summary: A user-friendly cross-platform GUI tool built with Tauri for sideloading iOS applications and managing device pairing files.
risk_notes: Requires installation of binary releases or building from source; interacts with Apple ID credentials and low-level device pairing files. It requires usbmuxd to communicate with iOS devices, which may require elevated permissions on some Linux distributions. Use with caution as it handles sensitive authentication data.

title: martichou/rquickshare
summary: A cross-platform Rust implementation of Android's Quick Share (formerly Nearby Share) for Linux and macOS, enabling seamless file transfers between mobile and desktop devices.
risk_notes: Distributed as pre-compiled binaries (deb, rpm, dmg) or via package managers like AUR/Nix. Requires network access for mDNS/LAN discovery and Bluetooth access for device discovery. Installation via dpkg/rpm requires root privileges. The project is actively maintained with frequent updates.

title: fengzeng/soia
summary: A high-performance, cross-platform media player built with Tauri and mpv that supports network streaming via WebDAV, DLNA, and SMB.
risk_notes: Distributed as pre-built binaries or via Homebrew/WinGet. It requires network access for streaming and stores network credentials in plain text within a local JSON file. It is a desktop application with standard user-level filesystem access; Linux support is currently limited to Wayland sessions.

title: gitbrent/pptxgenjs
summary: A robust, well-maintained JavaScript library for programmatically generating PowerPoint (.pptx) files in Node.js, browsers, and various frontend frameworks.
risk_notes: Installed via npm/yarn. It is a client-side/server-side library with no inherent network access or elevated privileges. It runs in the context of your application, so it only has access to the data you pass to it. It is actively maintained and widely used.

title: zidoro/pomatez
summary: A feature-rich, cross-platform desktop Pomodoro timer built with Electron, offering task management, strict mode, and system tray integration.
risk_notes: Distributed as a desktop application (AppImage, Snap, DMG, EXE). As an Electron app, it has access to standard user-level filesystem and system notifications. It includes auto-update functionality which fetches binaries from GitHub. No elevated privileges (sudo) required for installation via standard package managers like Homebrew or Snap.

title: ucybers/awesome-blackhat-tools
summary: A comprehensive, well-organized curated list of cybersecurity tools that have been officially presented at Black Hat conferences, categorized by region, year, and security domain.
risk_notes: This is a documentation-only repository containing links to external tools. It does not contain executable code itself. However, users should exercise caution when downloading and executing tools from the linked repositories, as many are offensive security tools that may require elevated privileges, network access, or interaction with sensitive systems.

title: visiondepth/visiondepth3d
summary: A proprietary, closed-source desktop application for AI-powered 2D-to-3D video conversion that uses this GitHub repository only for distribution and issue tracking.
risk_notes: The project is closed-source and distributed as a binary installer. It requires running untrusted proprietary code on your local machine, which may have full filesystem access. It is not a developer tool or library, but a commercial product with a restrictive license.

title: smgcommunity/petari
summary: A community-driven decompilation project for the game Super Mario Galaxy, focused on reverse engineering the original source code.
risk_notes: Requires manual compilation using build tools like Ninja and Python. It involves running third-party binary wrappers (Wine/Wibo) to execute Windows-based build tools on non-Windows systems. It does not contain game assets, requiring the user to provide their own legally obtained game files.

title: watzon/pindrop
summary: A native macOS menu bar dictation tool that leverages local AI models (WhisperKit) for private, offline speech-to-text with optional cloud-based enhancements.
risk_notes: Distributed as a signed/notarized DMG. Requires microphone access and optional accessibility permissions for text insertion. API keys for optional cloud services are stored in the macOS Keychain. The app is actively maintained and follows standard macOS security practices.

title: eliasdabbas/advertools
summary: A powerful Python library for digital marketing automation, SEO analysis, and data wrangling, designed with a modular, UNIX-like philosophy for easy integration into data pipelines.
risk_notes: Installed via standard 'pip install'. It is a library, not a standalone service, so it runs with the permissions of the user executing the script. It performs network requests (crawling, API calls) and file I/O. It is actively maintained and widely used in the SEO/data community.

title: rossant/awesome-math
summary: A comprehensive, community-curated list of high-quality mathematics resources, including learning platforms, lecture notes, and computational tools.
risk_notes: This is a documentation-only repository (a markdown list). There is no code to execute, install, or run, making it inherently safe from a security perspective. It is actively maintained.

title: dominux/pentaract
summary: Pentaract is a self-hosted cloud storage solution that uses the Telegram API as the underlying storage backend, allowing users to bypass traditional filesystem storage limits.
risk_notes: Requires Docker/Docker Compose for standard deployment. It relies on an external third-party service (Telegram) for data persistence, which introduces a dependency on Telegram's API terms and uptime. It requires a PostgreSQL database instance and sensitive environment variables (secrets/keys). The project is in early development and explicitly warns against production use.

title: autowarefoundation/autoware
summary: An enterprise-grade, complex open-source software stack for autonomous driving based on ROS 2.
risk_notes: Extremely heavy-duty software stack requiring significant hardware resources and complex build processes (often involving Docker and source compilation). It is not a typical home-lab tool and carries high operational complexity.

title: gommzystudio/device-activity-tracker
summary: A security research tool that demonstrates privacy vulnerabilities in WhatsApp and Signal by using RTT analysis of delivery receipts to track device activity states.
risk_notes: Requires Node.js and Docker. The tool requires authenticating with a personal WhatsApp account via QR code, granting the application access to your messaging metadata and contacts. It is a proof-of-concept for security research and should be used with caution regarding platform terms of service and privacy implications.

title: visualbruno/comfyui-trellis2
summary: A comprehensive ComfyUI wrapper for Microsoft's Trellis.2, enabling advanced 3D mesh generation, texturing, and remeshing workflows directly within the ComfyUI node-based environment.
risk_notes: Installs as a custom node within ComfyUI; requires manual installation of specific Python wheels and external model weights (e.g., DINOv3 from Hugging Face). It executes arbitrary Python code within the ComfyUI process, which has full access to your local filesystem and GPU. Requires careful dependency management (NATTEN, specific CUDA versions).

title: lorien/awesome-web-scraping
summary: A comprehensive, curated list of libraries, frameworks, and tools for web scraping across multiple programming languages.
risk_notes: This is a documentation-only repository (a list of links). There is no code to install or execute, so it carries no inherent security risk. Users should exercise caution when visiting external links or installing third-party scraping libraries listed within the repository.

title: stride3d/stride
summary: Stride is a cross-platform, open-source C# game engine featuring a visual editor and CLI tools for project management.
risk_notes: Installed via 'dotnet tool install -g', which places binaries in the user's PATH. Requires significant system resources and build tools (Visual Studio, C++ workloads). As a game engine, it has full access to the user's filesystem and network when running compiled projects.

title: antoniorodr/cronboard
summary: A terminal-based TUI dashboard for managing local and remote cron jobs with features like SSH support, job validation, and Telegram failure notifications.
risk_notes: Installed via pip/uv. Requires Python 3.13+. It interacts directly with the system crontab and requires SSH access (keys or passwords) to manage remote servers. Managing cron jobs for other users requires sudo privileges, which grants the tool significant system control.

title: valuecell-ai/valuecell
summary: ValueCell is a multi-agent platform designed for financial research and automated trading, supporting various LLM providers and major cryptocurrency exchanges.
risk_notes: Requires installation of a desktop application (MacOS/Windows) or use of their web platform. The application requires sensitive API keys for both LLM providers and cryptocurrency exchanges (Binance, OKX, Hyperliquid). Users must exercise caution as the software has the capability to execute trades on connected exchange accounts. The project is actively maintained but involves high-risk financial automation.

title: mobai-app/ios-builder
summary: A CLI tool that enables iOS development on non-macOS platforms by offloading builds to GitHub Actions and providing remote simulator/device integration via the MobAI service.
risk_notes: Installation via curl-to-bash is provided, which is a security risk; prefer Homebrew or binary downloads. The tool requires GitHub authentication and access to secrets for code signing. It relies on a third-party service (MobAI) for device/simulator integration, which requires an API key and potentially exposes your build artifacts to that service.

title: ente-io/ente
summary: A comprehensive, open-source, end-to-end encrypted platform providing alternatives to Google Photos, Authy, and secure document storage.
risk_notes: The project is highly active and has undergone multiple third-party security audits. Self-hosting requires managing a server (Docker/containerized deployment), which involves network exposure and storage management. Client apps are available via standard app stores or direct binaries, minimizing risky install patterns.

title: wkentaro/gdown
summary: A robust CLI tool and Python library for downloading files and folders from Google Drive, bypassing common issues like virus scan warnings and complex URL structures.
risk_notes: Installed via pip or uv. It requires network access to Google Drive and writes files to the local filesystem. It does not require elevated (root) privileges or API keys, as it mimics browser behavior for public links. The project is actively maintained.

title: 5rahim/seanime
summary: A comprehensive, self-hosted media server specifically designed for anime and manga, featuring robust library management, torrent integration, and cross-platform support.
risk_notes: Distributed as binaries or via source build; requires access to local media directories and network ports for the web interface. Integrates with third-party torrent clients and debrid services, which may require API keys. The project is actively maintained, but users should be aware of the security implications of running media servers with external torrent/debrid integrations.

title: vladsez/easy-invoice-pdf
summary: A privacy-focused, browser-based invoice generator that runs entirely client-side, ensuring no sensitive financial data is uploaded to a server.
risk_notes: The project is a web application that runs entirely in the browser (client-side), which is excellent for privacy. It does not require server-side installation or database access. As a static web app, it can be self-hosted via standard web servers (Nginx, Apache, etc.) or static site hosts. No sensitive credentials or root access are required.

title: cowtoolz/webcamize
summary: A C-based CLI tool for Linux that simplifies using external cameras (DSLRs, mirrorless, etc.) as webcams by orchestrating libgphoto2, ffmpeg, and v4l2loopback.
risk_notes: Requires root/sudo privileges for kernel module configuration (v4l2loopback) and device access. Installation involves compiling from source or using AUR, which requires system-level dependencies like libgphoto2 and ffmpeg. The project is actively maintained, but users should be aware that it modifies system video device drivers.

title: mudler/edgevpn
summary: A decentralized, serverless p2p VPN and reverse proxy built on libp2p, designed for creating secure tunnels and distributed networks without central infrastructure.
risk_notes: Installation via curl-to-shell script is provided, which carries inherent risks; manual binary download is recommended. As a VPN tool, it requires elevated privileges (root/sudo) to manage network interfaces and routing tables. The security model relies on shared tokens, and the documentation explicitly notes that some access control features are experimental.

title: guhcostan/mac-cleaner-cli
summary: An interactive, open-source CLI tool for macOS that safely identifies and removes junk files, caches, and development artifacts like Xcode DerivedData and node_modules.
risk_notes: Runs via npx (Node.js), which executes code from the npm registry. It requires filesystem access to scan and delete files in user directories. It is privacy-focused with no telemetry, but because it performs file deletions, it should be used with caution, especially when using the --risky flag.

title: kovacsv/online3dviewer
summary: A robust, open-source web-based 3D model viewer and converter that supports a wide range of CAD and 3D formats using Three.js.
risk_notes: The project is a client-side JavaScript library and web application. It can be self-hosted via npm or served as static files, posing minimal security risk as it runs entirely in the browser sandbox. No sensitive permissions or backend access are required for core functionality.

title: octelium/octelium
summary: A comprehensive, self-hosted zero-trust platform that combines VPN, ZTNA, API/AI gateway, and PaaS capabilities into a single unified infrastructure tool.
risk_notes: Requires significant infrastructure access as it functions as a gateway/proxy for internal networks and services. Installation typically involves binary deployment or containerized setup (Docker/Kubernetes). As a security-critical component, it requires careful configuration of policies and identity providers. The project is actively maintained, but users should audit the policy-as-code configurations to ensure they do not inadvertently expose internal resources.

title: eduard256/strix
summary: Strix is a powerful utility for discovering IP camera streams and automatically generating configuration files for Frigate and go2rtc.
risk_notes: Offers a curl-to-bash install script which requires root/sudo. Docker/Podman deployment requires host networking and specific capabilities (NET_RAW, NET_ADMIN) to perform network scanning. The tool interacts with local network devices and handles camera credentials, so it should be isolated within a trusted home network segment.

title: ggerganov/ggwave
summary: A lightweight C++ library for transmitting small amounts of data between devices using sound waves, useful for air-gapped communication and IoT pairing.
risk_notes: The library is a C++ header-only/source-based project with no dangerous install scripts. It requires access to system audio input/output devices (microphone/speakers). It is maintained by a highly active developer (ggerganov) known for high-quality C++ projects.

title: davidvkimball/vaultcms
summary: Vault CMS turns Obsidian into a headless CMS for Astro projects, featuring an automated CLI installer and an MCP server for AI-assisted content management.
risk_notes: Installs via standard npm/npx CLI which modifies local project files. Requires read/write access to your local filesystem (Obsidian vault). Includes an MCP server which allows LLMs to interact with your local content files; ensure your AI agent permissions are configured correctly.

title: spupuz/vibenvr
summary: A modern, containerized local NVR with advanced AI object detection, RBAC, and robust privacy features, designed for self-hosting.
risk_notes: Distributed as a Docker container, which is a standard and relatively safe deployment method. Requires access to local network camera streams (RTSP) and persistent storage for video files. Security features include JWT, OAuth, and 2FA, which are excellent for a self-hosted tool. Maintenance appears active with recent commits.

title: amebalabs/trex
summary: A high-quality macOS menu bar utility that provides offline OCR capabilities for extracting text from any screen area, including support for QR codes and automation.
risk_notes: Installed via Homebrew Cask or direct binary download. It requires macOS screen recording permissions to function. The project is actively maintained and operates entirely offline, minimizing privacy risks associated with cloud-based OCR services.

title: itsowen/cyberscraper-2077
summary: An AI-powered web scraping tool that leverages LLMs (OpenAI, Gemini, Ollama) for intelligent data extraction, featuring a Streamlit GUI, Tor support, and stealth capabilities.
risk_notes: Requires API keys (OpenAI/Gemini) or local Ollama access. Installation via pip or Docker. Uses Playwright, which can automate browser interactions; running with local browser instances or stealth modes carries inherent risks of triggering anti-bot protections or executing arbitrary site scripts. Maintenance appears active.

title: withoneai/cli
summary: A CLI tool that acts as a unified proxy for AI agents to interact with 600+ third-party APIs (Gmail, Stripe, etc.) without managing individual OAuth tokens.
risk_notes: Installed via npm/npx. It requires an API key from the provider and acts as a proxy for your credentials to third-party services, meaning you are trusting the provider's infrastructure with access to your connected accounts. It creates local configuration files in your home directory (~/.one).

title: algorithmicsuperintelligence/openevolve
summary: OpenEvolve is an advanced evolutionary coding agent framework that uses LLMs to autonomously discover and optimize algorithms, including GPU kernels and mathematical functions.
risk_notes: Installed via pip. Requires external LLM API keys (OpenAI/Gemini) to function. The tool executes generated code, which poses a significant security risk if the LLM produces malicious or destructive code; it should be run in a sandboxed environment or Docker container to prevent unauthorized filesystem or system access.

title: shaynep/local-voice-ai
summary: A comprehensive, containerized local voice AI assistant that orchestrates STT, LLM, and TTS services using LiveKit Agents.
risk_notes: Runs via Docker, which isolates the process, but requires mounting a volume for models and exposing network ports (8080, 7880, 7881, 7882/udp). The project manages multiple subprocesses; if running with GPU support, it requires the NVIDIA container toolkit. It is actively maintained and uses standard containerization practices.

title: infatoshi/cuda-course
summary: A comprehensive, high-quality educational repository for learning CUDA programming, GPU kernel optimization, and deep learning infrastructure.
risk_notes: This is an educational repository containing source code and documentation. It does not require installation via scripts; users typically clone the repo and compile C++/CUDA code locally using the NVIDIA CUDA Toolkit. It requires an NVIDIA GPU and standard development tools (gcc, nvcc). No inherent network or credential risks, but running custom kernels requires local hardware access.

title: maxritter/pilot-shell
summary: An orchestration layer for Claude Code and Codex CLI that adds spec-driven development, persistent memory, and quality gates to AI-assisted coding workflows.
risk_notes: Installs via a curl-to-bash script which executes with user permissions. It requires active subscriptions to Claude or Codex and integrates deeply with your local filesystem and shell environment to manage code, memory, and project configurations.

title: b16f00t/whapa
summary: A comprehensive forensic toolset for parsing, decrypting, and analyzing WhatsApp databases from Android and iOS, including support for cloud backups.
risk_notes: Requires local installation via pip; handles sensitive personal data (WhatsApp databases, cloud credentials). It is a local-only tool, but users should be cautious when providing cloud credentials (Google Drive/iCloud) to the configuration files. The project is actively maintained and uses standard Python dependencies.

title: bee-san/rustscan
summary: A high-performance, modern port scanner written in Rust that integrates seamlessly with Nmap for rapid network reconnaissance.
risk_notes: Requires network access to perform scans. Can be installed via standard package managers (brew, pacman) or cargo. As a security tool, it should be run with appropriate caution in a controlled environment. It is actively maintained and widely used in the security community.

title: celestoai/smolvm
summary: SmolVM provides a secure, high-performance infrastructure for running AI agents in isolated microVMs using Firecracker, QEMU, or libkrun.
risk_notes: Installation via 'curl | bash' is provided, which carries inherent security risks; manual pip installation is available. The tool requires root/sudo privileges to configure hypervisors (Firecracker/QEMU) and network interfaces. It is designed to handle untrusted code, but users should be aware that it manages host-to-guest file mounts and network egress, which could be misconfigured to expose host resources.

title: mxrch/ghunt
summary: A powerful OSINT framework for gathering information on Google accounts, Drive files, and BSSID geolocation.
risk_notes: Installed via pipx, which is a safe, isolated method. Requires authentication via browser cookies or a companion extension, which grants the tool access to your Google account session. Use with caution as it performs automated queries against Google services, which could trigger rate limits or account flags.

title: dwarvesf/hidden
summary: A popular, open-source macOS utility that allows users to hide and organize menu bar icons for a cleaner workspace.
risk_notes: Installed via Homebrew cask or App Store. As a GUI application, it requires accessibility permissions to interact with the menu bar. It is notarized by Apple, which provides a baseline of security verification. The project is actively maintained.

title: resumex/doom-over-dns
summary: A proof-of-concept project that demonstrates how to store and execute the Doom game engine entirely via DNS TXT records using PowerShell and Cloudflare's API.
risk_notes: Requires Cloudflare API tokens with DNS edit permissions. The script executes .NET assemblies directly into memory, which is a common pattern for fileless malware, though here it is used for a game engine. It requires PowerShell 7 and interacts with external DNS resolvers. It is a highly experimental project and not intended for production use.

title: khairul169/garage-webui
summary: A lightweight, self-hosted web management interface for the Garage distributed object storage system, providing bucket management, health monitoring, and access key administration.
risk_notes: Requires access to the Garage configuration file (which contains sensitive RPC secrets and admin tokens). Can be deployed via Docker or as a standalone binary. It requires network access to the Garage admin API and S3 endpoints. The project is actively maintained, but users should ensure the web UI is placed behind a reverse proxy with TLS, as it does not natively handle HTTPS.

title: linwooddev/butterfly
summary: A cross-platform, open-source note-taking and drawing application built with Flutter that supports local storage and WebDAV synchronization.
risk_notes: Distributed as binaries (AppImage, APK, Windows installer) or via web. It requires filesystem access to save notes locally and network access if using WebDAV for synchronization. The project is actively maintained and does not require elevated privileges or root access.

title: protongraph/protongraph
summary: A node-based procedural 3D content generation tool built as a Godot engine project.
risk_notes: Requires downloading and running via the Godot Engine editor. As a Godot project, it runs with the permissions of the Godot executable on your local filesystem. Maintenance is somewhat sporadic with a major port to Godot 4 in progress, which may lead to instability.

title: peternaame-boop/ytm-player
summary: A feature-rich terminal-based YouTube Music client built with Python and Textual, featuring vim-style keybindings, synced lyrics, and mpv integration.
risk_notes: Installed via pip or system package managers. Requires local authentication (browser cookie extraction) to access YouTube Music account data. Uses mpv as a backend, which is a standard media player. The project is actively maintained and includes a security policy.

title: sahandsafizadeh/qeep
summary: A deep learning framework written in Go that provides tensors, automatic differentiation, and CUDA-accelerated neural network components.
risk_notes: Requires CGO and local CUDA toolkit installation for GPU support. Installed as a Go module dependency. No inherent network access or elevated privilege requirements, but requires local compilation of C/CUDA code which introduces standard build-time risks.

title: idoka/awesome-canbus
summary: A comprehensive, well-maintained curated list of tools, hardware, and resources for CAN bus reverse engineering, security research, and automotive electronics.
risk_notes: This is a curated list of external links, not a single piece of software. Risks depend entirely on the specific tools selected from the list. Many tools listed require hardware interfaces (e.g., CAN-to-USB adapters) and may require root/sudo access to interact with SocketCAN interfaces on Linux. Users should exercise caution when running third-party scripts from these repositories as they often involve low-level hardware interaction.

title: eth-pbl/h-watch
summary: An open-source hardware project for a healthcare-focused smart watch featuring NB-IoT connectivity and various health sensors.
risk_notes: This is a hardware design project requiring custom PCB fabrication and assembly. It is not a software tool or CLI that can be installed on existing infrastructure. The project appears abandoned with no updates since early 2022.

title: brkgng/scrollsnap
summary: A native macOS utility for capturing and stitching scrolling screenshots using ScreenCaptureKit, featuring a customizable selection area and multi-language support.
risk_notes: The app is available via the Mac App Store or as a compiled binary from GitHub releases. It requires 'Screen Recording' permissions in macOS System Settings to function, which allows the app to capture content from other applications. The source code is available for audit, and it does not appear to require network access or elevated root privileges.

title: six2dez/reconftw
summary: A comprehensive, modular automation framework for security reconnaissance and vulnerability scanning that orchestrates various industry-standard tools.
risk_notes: The tool is a complex wrapper that installs and executes numerous third-party security binaries. It requires significant system permissions and network access to perform active scanning. Installation is typically done via shell scripts which may require sudo for dependency management. It is highly recommended to run this inside a dedicated Docker container or isolated VM to prevent host system contamination or accidental execution of malicious payloads against unauthorized targets.

title: chartgpu/chartgpu
summary: A high-performance, zero-dependency WebGPU charting library designed for large datasets, real-time streaming, and multi-chart dashboards.
risk_notes: Installed via npm/yarn as a standard frontend dependency. It runs entirely client-side in the browser using the WebGPU API, meaning it has no access to server-side files, network, or credentials beyond what the host application explicitly provides. It is actively maintained with no runtime dependencies, reducing supply chain risk.

title: marvinvr/docktail
summary: DockTail is a Go-based tool that automatically exposes Docker containers as Tailscale Services using label-based configuration, eliminating the need to publish container ports to the host.
risk_notes: Requires mounting the Docker socket (/var/run/docker.sock) and Tailscale socket (/var/run/tailscale) into the container, granting it significant control over the Docker daemon. It requires Tailscale OAuth credentials to manage services on your tailnet. The project is actively maintained and uses standard Docker deployment patterns.

title: runtipi/runtipi
summary: Runtipi is a user-friendly homeserver orchestrator that simplifies the deployment and management of self-hosted applications using a Docker-based web interface.
risk_notes: Installation typically involves a curl-to-bash script which requires root/sudo privileges to set up Docker and the management daemon. As an orchestrator, it has full access to the host filesystem and network to manage containers; users should be aware that it acts as a central control plane for all hosted services.

title: trykimu/videoeditor
summary: An open-source, AI-powered video editing platform built with React and Remotion, designed as a self-hostable alternative to Canva or Capcut.
risk_notes: Requires Docker for PostgreSQL and Nginx, plus Node.js and Python environments. Self-hosting involves managing sensitive credentials (BetterAuth secrets, Google OAuth, Gemini API keys) and exposing ports 80/443 if using a custom domain. The project is actively maintained but uses a dual-license model, so users should verify commercial usage terms.

title: wildminder/awesome-ai-voice
summary: A comprehensive, curated list of open-source Text-to-Speech (TTS), voice cloning, and audio generation models, organized by features and capabilities.
risk_notes: This is a documentation-only repository (a list of links). It does not contain executable code, so there are no direct security risks or installation requirements. However, the external models linked may require significant local compute resources (GPU) and dependencies (Python/PyTorch) to run.

title: mindee/doctr
summary: docTR is a high-performance, deep learning-based OCR library that provides seamless text detection and recognition for documents, supporting both PyTorch and TensorFlow backends.
risk_notes: Installed via pip (python-doctr). It is a library, so it runs within your application's process and has access to whatever files the user provides to it. It requires downloading pre-trained model weights from the internet upon first use. It is actively maintained by t2k GmbH.

title: mnh-jansson/open-battery-information
summary: A hardware-software toolkit designed to reset and repair locked Battery Management Systems (BMS) using an Arduino interface, helping to reduce electronic waste.
risk_notes: Requires physical hardware (Arduino) to interface with battery BMS. Software installation via pip or precompiled Windows binary. The software interacts directly with hardware via serial ports; users should be cautious when modifying BMS firmware as improper use could lead to battery failure or fire hazards.

title: ksimback/tech-debt-skill
summary: A specialized Claude Code skill that performs a comprehensive, file-cited technical debt audit of a codebase by integrating static analysis tools and architectural analysis.
risk_notes: Installation involves downloading a markdown file into a local ~/.claude/skills directory. The tool runs within the Claude Code environment, meaning it has read access to your entire repository and executes various language-specific analysis tools (e.g., ruff, cargo audit, npm audit) on your machine. It requires an active Claude Code setup and API access.

title: zubair-trabzada/ai-legal-claude
summary: A collection of AI agents and skills designed to integrate with Claude Code for legal document analysis and generation.
risk_notes: The installation uses a 'curl | bash' script, which is a significant security risk as it executes arbitrary code from the internet with the user's privileges. The tool is heavily marketed toward selling services via a 'Skool' community, suggesting it may be more of a lead-generation funnel than a robust, production-grade legal tool. It lacks a license, which is a major red flag for legal-related software.

title: blackprint/blackprint
summary: Blackprint is a visual programming framework that allows developers to create node-based logic flows, which can be exported as JSON and executed in various environments including browsers and Node.js.
risk_notes: Installed via npm (@blackprint/sketch). It is a client-side library, so it runs within the browser's sandbox or the Node.js runtime. It does not require root access, but if used for automation (e.g., Telegram bots), it will require access to sensitive API keys and network resources. The project is actively maintained.

title: achannarasappa/ticker
summary: A terminal-based TUI application for tracking stock and cryptocurrency prices, including support for position tracking and cost-basis calculations.
risk_notes: The tool requires network access to fetch financial data from public APIs. Installation methods include Homebrew, Snap, or manual binary download. The manual Linux install script uses sudo to move the binary to /usr/local/bin, which is a standard but privileged operation. It reads a local configuration file (~/.ticker.yaml) and does not require sensitive API keys or credentials to function.

title: ys-l/csvlens
summary: A high-performance, terminal-based CSV viewer written in Rust that provides an interface similar to 'less' for navigating, filtering, and searching large CSV files.
risk_notes: Low risk. It is a standalone binary with no network access requirements. It reads local files provided as arguments or via stdin. Installation is safe via standard package managers (brew, pacman, winget, cargo) or direct binary download. No special permissions or root access required.

title: frappe/builder
summary: A low-code, visual website builder built on the Frappe Framework, offering AI-powered page generation and seamless integration with the Frappe ecosystem.
risk_notes: Installation involves running a Python-based easy-install script or Docker Compose. As a full-stack CMS, it requires database access and handles web traffic, so it should be isolated in a containerized environment. The project is actively maintained by the Frappe team, a reputable organization in the open-source ERP space.

title: meigen-ai/posterreward
summary: PosterReward is a specialized reward model framework designed to evaluate the aesthetic and technical quality of AI-generated graphic design posters across five key dimensions.
risk_notes: Requires standard Python environment setup via Conda and pip. Uses vLLM for inference, which typically requires significant GPU resources and CUDA drivers. The code executes arbitrary model weights from Hugging Face, which should be treated as untrusted code execution. No specific root permissions are required, but it will access local filesystem for image processing and model caching.

title: edoardottt/scilla
summary: A versatile Go-based information gathering and reconnaissance tool for security testing, capable of DNS, subdomain, port, and directory enumeration.
risk_notes: Installs via standard package managers (brew, snap) or Go. Requires network access to perform scans. Can be configured with API keys for external services; users should exercise caution when running against targets they do not own or have explicit permission to test.

title: tabler/tabler-icons
summary: A comprehensive, high-quality collection of over 6,000 MIT-licensed SVG icons, widely used in web development and UI design.
risk_notes: Low risk. Distributed as standard npm packages or static SVG files. No special permissions, network access, or system-level execution required. Highly active maintenance.

title: microsoft/orchard
summary: Orchard is a high-performance, Kubernetes-native framework for agentic modeling, providing a shared environment substrate for training and evaluating AI agents across software engineering, browser navigation, and computer-use tasks.
risk_notes: This is a complex research framework designed for Kubernetes clusters. It requires significant infrastructure setup (Kubernetes, container orchestration) and involves running untrusted agent code within isolated containers. It is not a simple CLI tool; it is a heavy-duty backend service for training pipelines. Users should be aware of the security implications of running agentic code in containers, even if isolated.

title: prismer-ai/prismer
summary: An open-source research platform that integrates AI-driven paper reading, multi-agent orchestration, and LaTeX writing into a self-hostable workspace.
risk_notes: Requires Docker and Docker Compose for deployment. The application requires an OpenAI-compatible API key to function, which grants the platform access to your LLM usage and potentially sensitive research data. The project is actively maintained, but users should review the docker-compose configuration to understand the network exposure of the agent containers.

title: goclone-dev/goclone
summary: A high-performance website cloner written in Go that mirrors site structures locally, supporting custom user agents, cookies, and proxy configurations.
risk_notes: Installs via Homebrew or standard 'go install'. It requires network access to fetch external websites and writes files to the local filesystem. It does not require root privileges or sensitive API keys, but users should be mindful of the legal and ethical implications of scraping specific websites.

title: joaquinbejar/orderbook-rs
summary: A high-performance, thread-safe limit order book engine written in Rust, designed for low-latency trading systems and market simulations.
risk_notes: This is a library (crate) rather than a standalone application, so it carries no inherent network or filesystem risk until integrated into a project. It is installed via Cargo (Rust's package manager). As a low-level financial engine, it requires careful auditing of its concurrency logic if used in production trading environments.

title: thobiasn/tori-cli
summary: A lightweight, SSH-based Docker monitoring tool that provides metrics, logs, and alerting without requiring a heavy monitoring stack or exposed ports.
risk_notes: The installation uses a 'curl | sudo sh' script which is a common but high-privilege pattern. The agent requires access to the Docker socket and host /proc and /sys filesystems to function, which grants it significant visibility into the host. It is actively maintained and designed with a security-first approach by avoiding exposed network ports in favor of SSH tunneling.

title: kite-org/kite
summary: A modern, feature-rich Kubernetes dashboard that provides multi-cluster management, built-in AI assistance, and enterprise-grade security features like OAuth and RBAC.
risk_notes: Requires high-privilege access to Kubernetes clusters (via ServiceAccount/RBAC) to function. Installation is standard via Helm or Docker. As a dashboard with terminal access and cluster-wide management capabilities, it should be deployed behind a secure ingress with proper authentication (OAuth/MFA) enabled to prevent unauthorized cluster control.

title: alibaba/mnn
summary: MNN is a high-performance, lightweight deep learning inference engine optimized for on-device execution, including mobile, IoT, and edge hardware.
risk_notes: MNN is a C++ library typically integrated via build systems like CMake or Gradle. It does not require root access or external network calls by default, but users must be cautious when loading third-party model weights. It is highly active and maintained by a large organization.

title: comet-ml/opik-openclaw
summary: An official observability plugin for the OpenClaw agent framework that exports LLM traces, tool calls, and agent metadata to the Opik platform.
risk_notes: Installed via the OpenClaw CLI plugin manager. Requires an API key for the Opik platform and grants the plugin access to conversation data and tool call inputs/outputs, which may contain sensitive information. The plugin runs within the OpenClaw gateway process.

title: f/textream
summary: Textream is a versatile, open-source teleprompter application for macOS and iOS that offers word tracking, voice-activated scrolling, and various overlay modes for streamers and presenters.
risk_notes: Distributed via App Store, Homebrew (brew install textream), or GitHub releases. Requires microphone access for voice-activated features and speech recognition. It is a native macOS application with a clear privacy policy and active maintenance.

title: electerm/electerm
summary: A feature-rich, cross-platform terminal and multi-protocol client (SSH, SFTP, RDP, VNC) that includes AI integration and sync capabilities.
risk_notes: Distributed as a desktop application (Electron-based) via standard package managers like Homebrew, Snap, or direct binaries. It requires network access for remote connections and AI features. It handles sensitive credentials (SSH keys/passwords) and supports syncing configurations to third-party services, which requires careful management of your sync secrets.

title: lightbeam24/startube
summary: A userscript that modifies YouTube's interface, requiring a closed-source third-party client called V3 to function.
risk_notes: Requires installation via Tampermonkey/Violentmonkey. The script relies on 'V3', which the author explicitly states is closed-source, posing a significant security and privacy risk as it intercepts and modifies YouTube traffic and UI elements.

title: zen-logic/file-hunter
summary: A self-hosted, web-based file cataloging and deduplication tool that allows users to index offline storage media and manage large archives via a responsive UI.
risk_notes: Installation via curl-to-bash is provided, which is a security risk; manual download or Docker is safer. The application requires read/write access to the filesystems it catalogs and manages, and it runs a web server with user authentication. It is actively maintained and uses standard Python libraries.

title: nickbeth/wsl-usb-manager
summary: A lightweight Rust-based GUI wrapper for usbipd-win that simplifies managing and auto-attaching USB devices to WSL2 instances.
risk_notes: Distributed as a standalone Windows executable (.exe). It acts as a wrapper for the official usbipd-win tool, which requires administrative privileges to bind/attach USB devices. It does not appear to require network access or external API keys, but it interacts directly with system-level hardware drivers.

title: tuannvm/codex-mcp-server
summary: An MCP server that bridges Claude Code with the OpenAI Codex CLI, enabling AI-powered code analysis, reviews, and web search directly within your IDE.
risk_notes: Installed via npm (npx). Requires an OpenAI API key stored via the Codex CLI. As an MCP server, it has the potential to read/write files and execute commands in your workspace depending on how you configure the Claude Code/MCP permissions.

title: jaytel0/taste
summary: A pipeline tool that analyzes sets of reference images using vision models to generate a structured 'SKILL.md' file, which can be used to guide AI agents in producing consistent UI/UX designs.
risk_notes: Requires Node.js and npm to install dependencies. The local pipeline requires API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, or OpenRouter) stored in a local .env.local file. It reads images from a local directory and writes artifacts to a local .taste/ folder, posing minimal security risk beyond the potential for high API usage costs if not monitored.

title: mogenson/paperwm.spoon
summary: A tiling window manager plugin for Hammerspoon that brings scrollable, tiled window management to macOS.
risk_notes: Requires installation via git clone into the Hammerspoon Spoons directory. As a Hammerspoon plugin, it runs with the permissions granted to the Hammerspoon application, which typically includes Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions to manipulate windows. It is actively maintained and does not require network access or root privileges.

title: markrai/gitpow
summary: A cross-platform Git client built with Tauri and Rust, featuring unique ergonomics like image diff previews and customizable commit graph visualizations.
risk_notes: Requires building from source using Rust, Node.js, and wasm-pack. On Linux, it requires installing several system-level development libraries via sudo. As a Git client, it will have full read/write access to your local repositories and SSH/GPG keys configured for Git operations.

title: internetvin/internetvin-terminal
summary: An Obsidian plugin that provides a full-featured, multi-tabbed terminal emulator directly within the note-taking interface, specifically designed for macOS.
risk_notes: Installed via Obsidian's community plugin system (BRAT or manual zip). It runs as a plugin within the Obsidian process, meaning it has access to your vault files and inherits the permissions of the Obsidian application. It relies on macOS-specific PTY APIs and Python 3. No external network calls are explicitly required for core functionality, but it executes shell commands, which carries inherent risk if malicious commands are pasted into it.

title: caddyserver/xcaddy
summary: A specialized CLI tool for building custom Caddy web server binaries with third-party plugins, essential for self-hosting setups requiring specific modules.
risk_notes: Requires Go installed to build from source. Official binary releases are available. The tool interacts with the filesystem to generate binaries and requires network access to fetch Go modules. It is maintained by the official Caddy project, making it highly trustworthy.

title: freeman-jiang/beatsync
summary: A high-precision web-based audio synchronization engine that allows multiple devices to play audio in perfect sync using NTP-inspired protocols.
risk_notes: Requires Bun runtime for installation. The application runs as a web server and WebSocket service; it requires network access to coordinate devices. No sensitive system-level permissions are requested, but it is in early development, so security auditing is recommended before production deployment.

title: kafbat/kafka-ui
summary: A comprehensive, feature-rich web interface for managing and monitoring Apache Kafka clusters, supporting multi-cluster management, RBAC, and various cloud-native integrations.
risk_notes: Typically deployed via Docker/Docker Compose. It requires network access to your Kafka brokers and potentially sensitive credentials for Schema Registry or Cloud IAM. It is an active, well-maintained project, but as a management tool, it should be secured behind a reverse proxy or VPN and restricted via its built-in RBAC/authentication features.

title: mayneyao/eidos
summary: Eidos is a local-first, SQLite-based personal data management framework that provides a Notion-like interface for structured data, versioning, and automation via a CLI.
risk_notes: The CLI is installed via a curl-to-sh script, which carries inherent security risks; it is recommended to inspect the script before execution. The application operates on local files, meaning it requires filesystem access to the directories you designate as 'Spaces'. It is actively maintained and does not require cloud accounts for core local functionality.

title: opisek/luna
summary: Luna is a self-hosted calendar aggregator written in Go that consolidates CalDav, iCal, and Google Calendar feeds into a single customizable web interface.
risk_notes: The project is actively maintained but currently in pre-1.0 development. It requires network access to external calendar services and stores user credentials/calendar data, necessitating secure deployment practices. Installation is typically handled via Docker/Docker Compose, which is standard for self-hosting.

title: lissy93/portainer-templates
summary: A comprehensive, community-maintained collection of 500+ one-click deployment templates for Portainer, simplifying the setup of self-hosted services.
risk_notes: The project is a JSON configuration file consumed by Portainer. It does not execute code directly on your host. However, by adding this URL to Portainer, you are trusting the template definitions to pull and run Docker images from various sources. Ensure you review the images being deployed, as they may require network access, persistent storage, or environment variables containing sensitive credentials.

title: tastyigniter/tastyigniter
summary: A robust, Laravel-based open-source platform for restaurant management, online ordering, and table reservations.
risk_notes: Requires a standard LAMP/LEMP stack (PHP 8.3+, MySQL/MariaDB). Installation is typically via Composer, which is standard for PHP applications but requires careful management of web server permissions and database credentials. It is a complex web application that will be exposed to the internet, necessitating standard security hardening for web servers.

title: sastraxi/pgsh
summary: A CLI tool that enables Git-like branching workflows for local PostgreSQL databases, simplifying context switching and migration management.
risk_notes: Installed via npm/yarn global. It requires local access to PostgreSQL binaries (psql, pg_dump) and modifies your local .env files and database instances. It has not been updated since early 2023, suggesting it may be in maintenance mode, though it remains a useful utility for local development environments.

title: logisim-evolution/logisim-evolution
summary: A powerful, cross-platform digital logic design and simulation tool that supports VHDL and FPGA integration, ideal for hardware-focused home-lab projects.
risk_notes: Distributed as platform-specific installers (MSI, DMG, DEB, RPM) or a standalone Java JAR. As a desktop GUI application, it runs with user-level permissions and can access the local filesystem to save/load circuit files. It is a mature, actively maintained project, but users should be aware that running arbitrary Java JARs requires a JRE/JDK environment.

title: gorules/zen
summary: A high-performance, cross-platform business rules engine written in Rust that allows developers to decouple complex decision logic from application code using JSON-based decision models.
risk_notes: Installed as a library dependency via standard package managers (npm, pip, cargo). It is a pure logic engine that does not inherently require network access or elevated privileges, though it processes user-provided JSON decision models which should be treated as untrusted input if sourced from external users.

title: erev0s/vampi
summary: VAmPI is a intentionally vulnerable REST API designed for testing security tools and learning about OWASP API Top 10 vulnerabilities.
risk_notes: This is an intentionally vulnerable application. It should only be run in isolated environments (e.g., Docker containers or virtual machines) and never exposed to the public internet. It is distributed via Docker Hub and standard pip requirements, which is standard for security labs.

title: justnullname/quickview
